t:
Whole Account Excess of loss cover can be applied:-

I. In miscellaneous class of business wherein limits and priorities are set for each different sub-class
II. In reinsurance of legal liabilities to third parties
III. In protecting property risks loss exposures
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Aviation Excess of contracts uses which of the following methods for determining which claim falls within the scope of the excess of loss cover?

I. Losses occurring basis
II. Risk attaching basis
III. Premium basis
e: Correct answer: Only II (from the IC85 question bank).

t: The principal object of this Pool is to accept reinsurance and retrocession business from the African and Asian markets:-
e: Correct answer: F.A.I.R. (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
The excess of loss contract is not concerned with:-

I. Proportionate shares of the original sum insured
II. Premium and claims on any one risk
III. Amount of loss being reinsured
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
In Business Covered: Insuring clause non-proportional, if coverage is on 'each loss each risk' basis, there may be:-

I. A maximum limit per loss occurrence
II. A minimum limit per loss occurrence
III. An annual aggregate linked to the reinstatement provision
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Credit rating opinion does not take into account:-

I. Deductibles
II. Surrender or cancellation penalties
III. Timeliness of payment
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Adverse underwriting results of proportional treaties and resultant shrinkage of proportional reinsurance capacities, may force the reinsured to increase per risk retention levels, beyond what their financial strength may justify. Under such situations which form of reinsurance can provide protection for the increased retention levels?
e: Correct answer: Risk Excess of loss (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
What are the method/s for determining which claim falls within the scope of the "excess of loss cover and/or proportional treaties"?

I. "Losses occurring" basis
II. "Risk attaching" basis
III. "Premium earning" basis
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Which of the following statement best describes IBNR losses?
o: All losses occurring within the contract period ar
These refer to anticipated loss provisions in respect of individual claims which may take long time to get reported and even longer time to get fully settled
All premiums written by the reinsured during the c
It is the basis for rating working excess of loss
This assists the reinsurer to judge rating consist
e: Correct answer: These refer to anticipated loss provisions in respect of individual claims which may take long time to get reported and even longer time to get fully settled (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
As per currency clause, the settlement of balances are effected on the basis of:-

I. USD
II. Sterling pounds
III. Balances due in respective currencies
e: Correct answer: Only III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Lloyd's motor underwriters are recognised specialists in insuring the:-

I. Private cars
II. Motorcycles
III. High value vehicles
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Under which of the following method/s of calculating portfolio transfer, the premiums of the year are divided into twelve parts according to the month in which such premiums are ceded under the treaty?

I. 50% method
II. Twenty fourth system
III. Clean cut method
e: Correct answer: Only II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the risks in respect of which Personal Accident business carries catastrophe exposures.

I. Group PA policies
II. Passengers in a vehicle
III. Passengers in an aircraft
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Which of the following statement best describes surplus facultative reinsurance?
o: This reinsurance is intended to limit losses that
This form of reinsurance is mainly used in protect
This form of reinsurance may be affected on an individual risk where a one off' type of large loss may be expected to occur
This reinsurance protects a reinsured against an a
This form of reinsurance limits the aggregate amou
e: Correct answer: This form of reinsurance may be affected on an individual risk where a one off' type of large loss may be expected to occur (from the IC85 question bank).

t: XYZ Insurance Co. has fixed its retention limit at Rs. 10,00,000 for property insurance. The company has received a proposal for Rs. 1,00,00,000. What will be the 'surplus reinsurance' percentage?
e: Correct answer: 90% (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Normally an insurer or reinsurer starting to write reinsurance business will write ________________.
o: Both on Net lines and Gross lines
e: Correct answer: Only Net lines (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement.

I. The underwriting agencies are often run by brokers.
II. The captive companies are very often established in "tax haven".
III. Professional reinsurers either transact business on a direct basis with ceding companies or accept business through brokers.
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In non-proportional reinsurance Xs is the abbreviated form for _________.
e: Correct answer: Excess (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In "loss occurrence" clause, the duration and extent of any loss occurrence will be limited to what duration for earthquake?
e: Correct answer: 72 consecutive hours (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the problems faced by reinsurers who depend upon retrocession business.

I. Delayed remittances
II. Exchange losses
III. Stability of earning
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the relevant factor/s from following. Which is relevant in reinsurance programme design, to ensure prompt cover for the newer and increased exposures being added by new business?

I. Business development
II. Marketing plans
III. Investment and liquidity policy
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
In which of the following agreement/s, two parties agree to a specified trade in future at a specified time?

I. Futures
II. Forwards
III. Options
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
When a treaty is cancelled, where the profit commission is on an accounting year basis, it is normal practice for no profit commission statement to be rendered in which year?

I. The beginning of the year on which treaty was signed
II. The end of the anniversary year of treaty
III. The year on which treaty is cancelled
e: Correct answer: Only III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
In treaty reinsurance business:-

I. Administrative work will be low
II. Premium volume can be built up faster
III. Each offer will have to be scrutinised individually and either accepted or declined
e: Correct answer: Only II (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
While treaty reinsurance does not require review of individual risks by the reinsurer, it demands a careful review of: -

I. Underwriting philosophy of the ceding insurer
II. Practice and historical experience of the ceding insurer
III. Thoughtful evaluation of the ceding insurer's attitude towards claim management
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: ___________ provides a wider spread for the net retained portfolio of the insurer with an improved balance thus ensuring stability in profits.
e: Correct answer: Quota share treaty (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Which of the following things are not included in the 'bordereaux' list?

I. Name of the insured
II. Territorial scope
III. Class of risk
e: Correct answer: Only II (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In ____________, the underwriter will need to have an intimate knowledge of tariffs and other market conditions from which the business emanates.
e: Correct answer: Facultative reinsurance (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Given below are some of the functions of reinsurance. Identify the incorrect option.
o: Accumulation of claims under different classes
e: Correct answer: Erosion of solvency margins (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
In case of surplus reinsurance treaties, the bordereaux list gives details of:-

I. Premium rate
II. Amount reinsured
III. Period of insurance
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
For reinsurance accounts, the composition of risks ceded to each arrangement must be evaluated on the basis of:-

I. Cost of reinsuring
II. Local retentions
III. Loss ratios
e: Correct answer: Only III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Where a treaty covers more than one currency and/or class of business, then profit commission statement is prepared on:-

I. Accounting year basis
II. Underwriting year basis
III. Aggregate basis
e: Correct answer: Only III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Which of the following regulation relates the free reserves and assets of the insurer to the written premium income?
e: Correct answer: Solvency margin regulation (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In earlier times, in fire insurance, reinsurance contract was referred as:-
e: Correct answer: Guarantee policy (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
For which of the following under Miscellaneous accident business, normal method of reinsurance is surplus basis?

I. Personal Accident
II. Cash-in-Transit
III. Burglary
e: Correct answer: I,II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Which of the following statement best describes "Gross Net premium Income"?
o: All losses occurring within the contract period ar
Under this method, claims under policies issued or
All premiums written by the reinsured during the contract period less return premiums, cancellations, premiums on excluded risks and premiums on reinsurances which reduce the reinsurer's exposure
It is the basis for rating working excess of loss
This assists the reinsurer to judge rating consist
e: Correct answer: All premiums written by the reinsured during the contract period less return premiums, cancellations, premiums on excluded risks and premiums on reinsurances which reduce the reinsurer's exposure (from the IC85 question bank).

t: This clause brings out clearly the obligatory nature of reinsuring, in that the insurer binds himself to cede and the reinsurer binds himself to accept:-
e: Correct answer: Operative clause (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
When reinsurances are ceded and accepted it is important to establish the credit rating of the reinsurer with reference to his:-

I. Business continuity
II. Ability to settle
III. His country's foreign exchange position
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Which of the following investment/s helps in increasing corporate liquidity?

I. Long term investments
II. Stock market investments
III. Investments in liquid assets
e: Correct answer: Only III (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In India, IRDAI has stipulated the use of reinsurers with rating _______________
e: Correct answer: Not less than BBB (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Some ______________ are owned by large composite companies or other industrial / commercial concerns but operate independently from the parent insurer.
e: Correct answer: Professional reinsurance companies (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to Excess of loss cover.

I. The status of the ceding insurer is that of a reinsured.
II. Ceding insurer does not cede risk and proportional premium.
II. Ceding insurer seeks protection to mitigate a loss beyond his chosen limit of loss retention.
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement.

I. Management of an insurer set the retention limits at a level they can afford to risk their solvency.
II. If management sets retention limits too low, they expose themselves to retaining more when claims occur.
III. If the retention limits are set high they may find they are ceding too large a part of their premium income to their reinsurers.
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
The crucial role of reinsurance is in: -

I. Addressing the limitations to the law of large numbers
II. Preserving the income from investment
III. Insulating shareholders' funds from unpredictable loss scenarios
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
At the end of the accounting year, a provision is required to be made for:-

I. Estimated profit
II. Estimated expenses
III. Outstanding losses
e: Correct answer: Only III (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
Standard fire insurance belongs to which class of insurance?

I. Property reinsurance
II. Marine reinsurance
III. Aviation reinsurance
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t:
For estimated losses, in cases where there is a provision for portfolio entry in the treaty concerned:-

I. The same amount is to be included as estimate for outstanding claims
II. The trend of incurred claims ratios over a period would assist to estimate the incurred claims for the current year and a provision for outstanding claims can be made after deducting the paid claims for the year
III. The underwriter may also decide to make an additional "ad hoc" provision for claims Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR)
e: Correct answer: Only I (from the IC85 question bank).

t: In the event of the reinsured's net loss ratio for a given year rises above a certain percentage, __________________ reinsurance in excess of that figure up to a higher agreed percentage beyond which the reinsured retains the loss.
e: Correct answer: Stop loss (from the IC85 question bank).

t: _____________ are used to reduce the insurer's loss in respect of a single risk .
e: Correct answer: Retention per risk (from the IC85 question bank).

t: Which of the following statement is TRUE with regard to Working (Risk) Excess of loss reinsurance?
o: This reinsurance is intended to limit losses that arise on the reinsured's day-to-day operations
This form of reinsurance is mainly used in protect
This form of reinsurance may be affected on an ind
This reinsurance protects a reinsured against an a
This form of reinsurance limits the aggregate amou
e: Correct answer: This reinsurance is intended to limit losses that arise on the reinsured's day-to-day operations (from the IC85 question bank).
